slate_hud.name: Slate HUD
slate_hud.settings.section.hud.about: The game's own HUD in Slate's look: the hotbar, the effects and the held item's name, and the experience bar and the boss bars on a ground in Slate's tones. Hearts, armour and hunger stay the game's icons unless you switch Slate's bars on below. Everything stays where the game has it.
slate_hud.settings.vanilla_note: The style is set to Vanilla, so the HUD is the game's own. These settings apply with the Slate style (Interface, Look).
slate_hud.settings.enabled.tip: Off: the whole HUD is the game's own, whatever is switched on below.
slate_hud.settings.effectTime.tip: A line along the foot of an effect's plate that runs out as the effect does. It turns amber for the last ten seconds.
slate_hud.settings.yieldToMods.tip: A part another installed mod draws itself is left to that mod: Better Inventory's hotbar, the hearts of a mod that stacks or recolours them. Off: Slate draws every part that is switched on.
slate_hud.settings.appleSkin.tip: What AppleSkin knows, in Slate's look: saturation as a line under the hunger bar, exhaustion as a faint line over it, and what the food in hand would restore as a pale stretch of the hunger and health bars. It applies while Slate's hunger and health bars are switched on. Off: AppleSkin draws its own icons over the bars.
slate_hud.settings.section.parts.about: A part that is off is drawn by the game, exactly as without Slate HUD. The bars for health, armour, hunger, air and a mount's health are off unless you switch them on: the game's icons show. So are the parts the game has nothing of, from the pickup feed on.
slate_hud.settings.left_to.tip: %s draws this part itself, so Slate leaves it alone. Switch off "Leave parts to other mods" to have Slate draw it anyway.
slate_hud.settings.part.hotbar.tip: The nine slots, the mark on the selected one, the off-hand slot and the attack indicator beside the hotbar.
slate_hud.settings.part.health.tip: A bar in place of the game's hearts, a cell for each heart. Absorption follows in gold; poison, wither and frost change the colour; a hardcore world reddens the frame. Off: the game's hearts.
slate_hud.settings.part.armor.tip: A low bar over health in place of the game's armour icons, while armour is worn. Off: the game's icons.
slate_hud.settings.part.hunger.tip: A bar in place of the game's shanks, a cell for each, filling from the right as the game's row does. Off: the game's shanks.
slate_hud.settings.part.air.tip: A bar in place of the game's bubbles for the air left under water. Off: the game's bubbles.
slate_hud.settings.part.mountHealth.tip: A bar in place of the hearts of what you ride, where hunger otherwise is. Off: the game's hearts.
slate_hud.settings.part.jumpBar.tip: The charge of a horse's jump (and a camel's dash), where the experience bar otherwise is: the game's own bar on a ground in Slate's tones.
slate_hud.settings.part.experience.tip: The game's own experience bar on a ground in Slate's tones. What fills the bar and the level over it stay the game's.
slate_hud.settings.part.effects.tip: The status effects in the upper right corner.
slate_hud.settings.part.itemName.tip: The name that shows for a moment when the item in hand changes.
slate_hud.settings.part.bossBar.tip: The game's own boss bars on a ground in Slate's tones, the name on a pill. The colour that fills a bar and its notches stay the game's, and the bars stay where the game has them.
slate_hud.settings.part.pickups.tip: A short line at the right edge of the screen for what you pick up or are given: the item, its name and how many. More of the same add up in one line, and experience has a line of its own. The game has nothing like it, so it is off unless you switch it on.
slate_hud.settings.part.healthBars.tip: A bar over a creature's head in the world, showing how much health it has left. Which creatures have one is chosen under Health bars below. The game has nothing like it, so it is off unless you switch it on.
slate_hud.settings.part.damageNumbers.ti: How much a hit took, as a number that rises from where the hit was: the hits you deal (amber for a critical one), and the ones you take in red. The game has nothing like it, so it is off unless you switch it on.
slate_hud.settings.part.compass.tip: A compass strip at the top of the screen, with your waypoints on it. It stands under the boss bars when there are any. The game has nothing like it, so it is off unless you switch it on.
slate_hud.settings.part.crosshair.tip: Slate's crosshair, shaped and coloured as you set it under Crosshair below. Off: the game's own. The attack indicator under it stays the game's.
slate_hud.settings.section.healthBars.ab: Bars over creatures in the world. The creature you aim at and those you hit in the last few seconds always have theirs. A bar is hidden behind walls as the creature is, and grows with the distance so it stays readable.
slate_hud.settings.healthBarsShow.tip: Monsters: hostile creatures. All creatures: everything that lives but armour stands, other players too. The one you aim at: only the creature your crosshair is on.
slate_hud.settings.healthBarsHurt.tip: A creature at full health has no bar. The one you aim at and those you just hit always have one.
slate_hud.settings.healthBarsRange.tip: How far away a creature's bar still shows.
slate_hud.settings.healthBarsSize.tip: How large the bars are. At 100% a bar up close is about the size of a name over a head.
slate_hud.settings.section.damageNumbers: Numbers in health points, read from what the server tells the game: they work on any server. Within 32 blocks.
slate_hud.settings.damageNumbersTaken.ti: Hits on you have their numbers too, in red. In the first person they rise left of the crosshair.
slate_hud.settings.damageNumbersAll.tip: What other creatures nearby do to each other has its numbers too, in a quieter colour.
slate_hud.settings.damageNumbersSize.tip: How large the numbers are, against the other words of the HUD.
slate_hud.settings.section.compass.about: Half the horizon from edge to edge, north in the accent. A waypoint you face names itself under the strip with its distance; one beyond the edge waits there, fainter.
slate_hud.settings.compassWaypoints.tip: The places Slate puts on your maps (homes, warps, the spawn, your team's home, as chosen in Places on maps) and, with Xaero's Minimap installed, the waypoints it shows in this world.
slate_hud.settings.compassWidth.tip: How wide the strip is, in pixels of the interface. It holds half the horizon at any width. 182 is the width of the boss bars and the hotbar.
slate_hud.settings.compassDown.tip: How far under its place the compass stands, in pixels of the interface: its place is at the top of the screen, or under the boss bars when there are any.
slate_hud.settings.section.crosshair.abo: Your crosshair at its true size over the grounds it has to read on. Changes show at once.
slate_hud.settings.crosshairStyle.tip: A cross with a gap in the middle, the same with a dot in it, a dot, a ring with a dot, or a T (a cross without its upper arm).
slate_hud.settings.crosshairInvert.tip: Drawn the way the game draws its own crosshair: what lies behind it turned inside out, so it reads on anything. The colour and the rim are then not used.
slate_hud.settings.crosshairOutline.tip: A dark rim of one pixel round the crosshair, so it reads on bright and dark grounds alike.
slate_hud.settings.crosshairSize.tip: How long the arms are, in pixels of the interface. For the ring, how large it is.
slate_hud.settings.crosshairGap.tip: How wide the gap in the middle is, in pixels of the interface.
slate_hud.settings.crosshairThickness.ti: How heavy the lines are, in pixels of the interface. For the dot, how large it is.
slate_hud.settings.section.hidden.about: Parts of the game's HUD you do not want to see at all. A hidden part is drawn neither by Slate nor by the game while the Slate style is on; other mods' additions stand where they would without it.
slate_hud.settings.hide.tip: On: this part of the HUD is not drawn at all. Off: it shows, in Slate's look or the game's as the Parts section says.
